To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the cross section for coherent diffractive production in the minijet region is ∝ A2 and the cross section for incoherent production of minijet pairs is ∝ A4.
the coherent diffractive dissociation cross section is proportional to A2 in the kinematical region 1 GeV < pT < 3 GeV and that shadowing is a leading twist effect.

the nuclear dependence of coherent diffractive production in the minijet region is proportional to A2 in the kinematical region where the minijet cross section is dominated by the leading-twist term; the leading correction to this behavior is a positive term proportional to A7/3 caused by nuclear shadowing and multiple scattering; shadowing reappears as an A2 leading-twist effect in the Tev energy range.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the physics of coherent diffractive production in nuclear collisions.
the study of nuclear shadowing and coherent diffraction of mesons and photons in the hard QCD regime.
the study of the production of jets of hadrons in high-energy nuclear collisions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the nuclear diffractive minijet cross section is dominated by a color transparency effect.
the cross section for coherent diffractive minijet production is proportional to A2, and that the leading correction is a positive term ∝ 1 A 2 7 3, and the next leading correction is ∼ A 2 5 3.
the cross section for coherent hard diffraction is proportional to A 2 in the region of large transverse momentum, and to A2/3 for the region of small transverse momentum.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nuclear dependence of the coherent diffractive cross section is dominated by the color transparency effect.
the cross section for hard diffractive production in nuclei is proportional to the square of the number of nucleons, with a leading correction ∝ A 2 3.
the nuclear shadowing effect in the Tev energy range is not the same as the shadowing effect in low energy range.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the nuclear modification of the coherent diffractive cross section for minijet production can be used to probe color transparency in the hard scattering of quarks and gluons.
the coherent production of high-pT minijets is a very promising way to test the color transparency phenomenon in the nuclear medium.

the coherent nuclear production of minijet pairs is an ideal tool for studying color transparency, which is the suppression of the nuclear absorption of hard processes due to the small size of their color flux tubes.
